sections.h2: What sets a Wildwood, MO sale apart?
sections.html:
Wildwood covers about 67 square miles at the western edge of St. Louis County. A seller here deals with St. Louis County for building records, inspections and tax bills, and with the city itself for zoning and, in the case of rentals, occupancy permits. Owner-occupied sales do not need an occupancy permit.

The July 2025 Census estimate is 34,955 people, slightly under the 35,417 counted in 2020. The 2020 density was 531.5 people per square mile, against 5,967.5 in University City, so lot size and space between neighbors weigh more here.

sections.h2: Where is Wildwood, and when did it become a city?
sections.html:
Wildwood is in the far western part of St. Louis County. It was incorporated on September 1, 1995. It covers 67.08 square miles, including 0.66 square miles of water. Chesterfield is to the north, Clarkson Valley and Ellisville to the east, Eureka and Pacific to the south, and Franklin County to the west.

Parks shape the area. Hikers use the Al Foster Trail inside the city and head to nearby Rockwoods Reservation and Babler State Park. The Big Chief Restaurant, a remnant of a tourist complex opened on U.S. Route 66 in 1928, has been on the National Register since 2003.

Most of Wildwood belongs to the Rockwood School District, and Lafayette High School is within the city limits. A small part lies in the Meramec Valley School District. St. Louis Community College has a Wildwood campus off Routes 100 and 109. The city contracts with the St. Louis County Police Department for police service.

Wildwood posts higher home values, incomes and owner shares than University City, Wentzville or Springfield.

Owners live in 91.8 percent of homes, so rentals are scarce and most buyers expect to live in the house. The 2020 census put the median age at 44.1, with married couples making up 73.4 percent of households.

That census counted 12,481 households among 12,918 housing units, of which 3.4 percent stood empty. Vacancy among owned homes was 1.1 percent. People 65 and older are 20.7 percent of residents.

sections.h2: Is an occupancy permit needed to sell a Wildwood house?
sections.html:
No, not when the house is owner-occupied. Wildwood's residential occupancy permit applies only to non-owner-occupied homes, and the city's program lists an effective date of March 1, 2025. An occupancy permit and inspection are required when the occupant of a rental or other non-owner-occupied house changes, and new construction or owner-occupied homes do not need an inspection or permit.

  • The inspection is performed by St. Louis County Public Works, and a passed inspection is not a permit by itself.
  • The city's permit fee is $40, or $20 to update occupants, and the application can go through the city's MyGov portal.
  • The inspection fee covers the first visit and a second one; each extra visit costs $50.
  • The application lapses after 90 days if noted deficiencies are not corrected.
  • The unit must be vacant when the inspector arrives.

That affects a sale to an investor who intends to rent, since the new tenant waits for the permit. Metro West Fire Protection District also requires its own inspection within its service area, while the city's page says the Eureka and Monarch districts do not require one for single-family homes. Confirm with your fire district, since that can change.

sections.h2: Which Wildwood permits and city rules touch a property?
sections.html:
If a buyer or seller wants to change the house before closing, the city's Planning Department at 16860 Main Street, phone 636-458-0440, handles zoning authorization. Fences, decks, sheds, pools and retaining walls all need at least zoning authorization. Building permits follow the St. Louis County building code, and the county Public Works office takes calls at 314-615-2559.

  • Building permits cover additions, new construction, electrical and mechanical work, plumbing, structural changes, above-ground pools and some retaining walls.
  • Utility sheds of 120 square feet or less and fences under six feet skip the building permit but keep the zoning authorization.
  • Grass over 10 inches is a nuisance under the city's code enforcement rules.
  • Bins have to stay out of sight from the street in front of the house.

Utilities vary by address: Missouri American Water supplies water, MSD Project Clear provides sewer service, and trash is collected by Republic Services in urban areas or Gateway Disposal on rural and private roads. Residents 65 and older can get a 15 percent trash discount by contacting the hauler. Tell your buyer which hauler serves the address.

sections.h2: What should I gather before listing a Wildwood house?
sections.html:
Collect the paperwork a buyer or an investor will ask for, starting with the county tax account and any permit history for decks, pools, sheds or retaining walls. Wildwood's Planning Department can tell you whether past work carried zoning authorization.

  • The name of your fire district, since Metro West, Monarch and Eureka serve different parts of the city and only some of them inspect single-family homes.
  • Your trash hauler, either Republic Services or Gateway Disposal, and whether you qualify for the 65-plus discount.
  • Who maintains your road, which may be Wildwood, St. Louis County, MoDOT or a neighboring city.
  • Your streetlight owner, because the city maintains lights only in the Town Center Zoning District and Ameren Missouri handles most others.

The city's FAQ notes that Republic Services serves urban areas while Gateway Disposal covers rural areas and private roads, and the 2020 census counted 23.1 percent of residents as rural. Put those details in your listing so buyers know what service the address gets.

The city's FAQ says St. Louis County manages all property taxes. For each bill the cutoff is a December 31 payment or postmark, and the county Collector says later payments carry interest of up to 18 percent a year plus a 2 percent penalty under RSMo chapters 139 and 140. The Collector's office is in Clayton at 41 S. Central Avenue; call (314) 615-7100, or (314) 615-7865 for back taxes.

Every odd-numbered year the County Assessor revalues all real estate, so the next round is 2027. Value appeals go to the Board of Equalization between May 1 and the second Monday in July, and July 13, 2026 has gone by. If back tax is owed, the settlement statement should show it deducted from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell in Wildwood?
sections.html:
Some owners need a quick sale because of a move, an estate or repairs, and others have time to prepare. Here are the common paths.

  • List with an agent. Get the commission quoted in writing, and budget for repairs a buyer's inspector may raise.
  • Sell by owner. You control the price and the showings and also take on the contract and disclosures.
  • Sell to an investor. An investor may buy the house in its current state and close on your date. Put the written offer next to your likely net from a listing.

Before you list, find out who maintains your road. The city's FAQ says a street may belong to Wildwood, St. Louis County, MoDOT or another municipality, and the Public Works office will help you find the right contact.

faqs.q: Does Wildwood require an occupancy permit when I sell my home?
faqs.a: No, not for an owner-occupied home. The permit applies to non-owner-occupied properties when the occupant changes, and the program's effective date was March 1, 2025.

faqs.q: How much is the Wildwood residential occupancy permit?
faqs.a: The city fee is $40, or $20 to update occupants. The inspection through St. Louis County is separate, and each visit after the second costs $50.

faqs.q: Which government bills property tax in Wildwood?
faqs.a: St. Louis County, through its Collector of Revenue in Clayton. Each year's bill is due by December 31.
Rockwood covers most of the city and Lafayette High School stands inside it. A small corner belongs to the Meramec Valley district.

faqs.q: How high are Wildwood home values?
faqs.a: Owners reported a median of $495,800 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $161,060 and 91.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied.
